title: The History of Tomb Raider | From Core Design To Lara Croft Reboots | Gaming History
description: The full history of Tomb Raider: Lara Croft's 1996 debut at Core Design, The Angel of Darkness, the Crystal Dynamics reboots, the Survivor trilogy, films and the new games announced in 2025.

sections.heading: Lara Croft arrives
sections.script: Twin pistols, a braided ponytail and a love of ancient tombs. Lara Croft is one of the most recognisable characters in gaming, and her adventures have been going for almost thirty years. Guinness World Records lists her as the best selling videogame heroine, and the Tomb Raider series has passed one hundred million copies sold. In this video we follow the full history of Tomb Raider, from a British studio's bold three dimensional experiment in nineteen ninety six, to the bumpy years that nearly ended the series, the reboots of two thousand six and two thousand thirteen, the films and shows, and the new games announced in December twenty twenty five. Pack your climbing gear and watch your footing, because the floor here is not always solid.

sections.heading: Core Design and the first game
sections.script: The story begins at Core Design, a British developer owned by the publisher Eidos Interactive. Work on the first Tomb Raider began in nineteen ninety four, and the game came out in nineteen ninety six, first on the Sega Saturn and then on the PlayStation and personal computers. It put you in a huge three dimensional world with a character who could run, jump, climb, swim and dive in any direction. Instead of fast shooting, it asked you to solve puzzles and find your way across giant caverns. The game became a sensation, and Lara Croft turned into a pop culture icon almost overnight. The success meant that the studio was soon asked to make another one, and then another, as quickly as possible.

sections.heading: One game every year
sections.script: After the hit, Core Design made a new Tomb Raider almost every single year. Tomb Raider two came in nineteen ninety seven and Tomb Raider three in nineteen ninety eight. Then came The Last Revelation in nineteen ninety nine, which ended with Lara apparently trapped under a collapsing pyramid, and Chronicles in the year two thousand. A deal with Sony kept the console versions on PlayStation for a time, until the end of the exclusivity deal in two thousand. The yearly pace was hard on the staff, and former team members have said that the pressure left them exhausted. By the end of Chronicles, many felt that the series needed a longer break and a fresh idea. They would get the break, but it would not be a smooth one.

sections.heading: The Angel of Darkness stumbles
sections.script: The sixth game, Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness, was meant to be a bold new start for the PlayStation 2. It launched in June two thousand three after delays, with a darker city setting, more stealth and a second playable character. Unfortunately, it was released with many bugs and mixed reviews, and it was considered a failure. A planned sequel was scrapped, and Eidos moved the series to another developer, the American studio Crystal Dynamics, who had begun production in two thousand four. Core Design later left the franchise, and the studio was ultimately shut down in two thousand ten. It was a sad end for the team that created Lara, but it opened the door for a new era, and one of the most successful comebacks in the series.

sections.heading: Legend, Anniversary and Underworld
sections.script: Crystal Dynamics relaunched the series with Tomb Raider: Legend in April two thousand six. The game rebuilt Lara's movement and look, and her original creator, Toby Gard, helped on the project. Legend was followed by Tomb Raider: Anniversary in two thousand seven, a remake of the first game using the same engine, and Tomb Raider: Underworld in two thousand eight. These games told a connected story about Lara's missing mother and her father's research, and they were praised for smoother controls and cinematic action. Square Enix bought Eidos in two thousand nine and took over the series. Lara also starred in smaller spin offs, such as Guardian of Light in twenty ten, which was a top down co op adventure. Still, the team was already preparing something very different.

sections.heading: A younger Lara
sections.script: In twenty thirteen, Crystal Dynamics rebooted the series again with a game simply called Tomb Raider. It showed a younger and more vulnerable Lara, shipwrecked on a dangerous island called Yamatai on her first expedition. The game was an origin story that mixed survival, bow combat, climbing and a more realistic tone. Camilla Luddington voiced Lara in this version. The game sold millions, and by the following year the publisher reported that it had passed eight and a half million copies worldwide, which at the time made it the best selling Tomb Raider. It was an important comeback and brought a new generation of fans into the series, after the long gap since the previous game.

sections.heading: Rise and Shadow
sections.script: The second game of the new trilogy, Rise of the Tomb Raider, came out in two thousand fifteen on Xbox consoles first, as part of a timed deal with Microsoft, and reached PlayStation 4 and computers in twenty sixteen. It sent Lara to Siberia and added crafting and larger open areas to explore. The final chapter, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, followed in September twenty eighteen on PlayStation 4, Xbox One and computers. It took Lara through Peru and focused on survival, jungle exploration and optional tombs. Together, the three games make up what fans call the Survivor trilogy, telling how Lara turns from a scared student into the fearless adventurer everyone knows. After that, the series went quiet for a time.

sections.heading: Films, shows and remasters
sections.script: Lara has also been a movie star. Angelina Jolie played her in two films, Lara Croft: Tomb Raider in two thousand one and The Cradle of Life in two thousand three. Alicia Vikander took over in a reboot film in twenty eighteen. An animated series, Tomb Raider: The Legend of Lara Croft, appeared on Netflix in October twenty twenty four, and a live action series for Prime Video is in the works with Phoebe Waller Bridge. In twenty twenty two, Embracer Group bought Crystal Dynamics, Eidos and the franchise from Square Enix. The company announced in October twenty twenty four that the series had passed one hundred million copies sold. Meanwhile, remasters of the original six games came out in two collections, in twenty twenty four and twenty twenty five.

sections.heading: What comes next
sections.script: At The Game Awards in December twenty twenty five, Crystal Dynamics and Amazon Game Studios revealed two new games, both built in Unreal Engine five. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is a remake of the nineteen ninety six original, made together with the studio Flying Wild Hog. Tomb Raider: Catalyst is a brand new adventure that takes Lara to northern India, with a planned release in twenty twenty seven. Both games feature Alix Wilton Regan as the voice of Lara. We will treat the release plans with care, since dates can change, so please check the official channels for the latest news. Still, it is a good sign for a series that has spent almost thirty years climbing out of one trap after another.

sections.heading: Your favourite Lara
sections.script: Looking back, Tomb Raider's journey is a rare one. It started with a daring three dimensional idea, grew into a worldwide phenomenon, stumbled badly, and then reinvented itself twice. It gave us puzzle filled tombs, huge set pieces and a heroine who has stayed popular across three decades. So here is our question. Which era of Lara Croft do you like best: the classic Core Design games, the Legend trilogy, or the Survivor trilogy, and which tomb is your favourite? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, please subscribe for more franchise stories. Thanks for watching, and remember to look before you leap.
